ticket.commented: Resolving Recipients Once

Who should hear about a new comment — the customer plus opted-in watchers, minus whoever just wrote it — worked out once, here, not by every listener.

ticket.commented needs to answer a question the other three events don't: who cares about this comment? The domain model has an answer — the ticket's customer, plus any watcher whose TicketWatcher.notifyOnComment is true — but resolving that answer takes two more queries, and doing it separately in each of three listeners would mean three copies of the same logic, and three times the database load for one comment:

// Figure 5.5: resolving recipients before ever emitting (src/services/comment.service.js, excerpt)
const ticket = await prisma.ticket.findUnique({
  where: { id: ticketId },
  select: {
    id: true,
    subject: true,
    customerId: true,
    watchers: { where: { notifyOnComment: true }, select: { userId: true } },
  },
});

const recipientIds = new Set([ticket.customerId, ...ticket.watchers.map((w) => w.userId)]);
recipientIds.delete(authorId);

const recipients = recipientIds.size
  ? await prisma.user.findMany({
      where: { id: { in: [...recipientIds] } },
      select: { id: true, name: true, email: true },
    })
  : [];

domainEvents.emit(EVENTS.TICKET_COMMENTED, { comment, ticket: { id: ticket.id, subject: ticket.subject }, recipients });

A Set is what makes recipientIds.delete(authorId) a one-line way to answer "everyone who should hear about this, except whoever just wrote it" — the customer might be the comment's author (replying on their own ticket), or a watcher might be, and either way they should be silently excluded, not notified about their own comment. watchers: { where: { notifyOnComment: true } } filters out opted-out watchers before the Set is even built, so nothing downstream has to check that flag again.

The resolved recipients — full { id, name, email } rows, not just ids — go straight into the event payload alongside comment and a trimmed-down ticket. Every listener in the next few topics can loop over recipients directly; none of them re-queries Prisma to find out who a name or email belongs to. This whole block is also wrapped in its own try/catch in the real file — the comment itself is already committed by this point, so a failure resolving recipients must never turn an already-successful comment into a failed request. The next topic's listeners lean on that same reasoning for a different reason.
